questionText: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the passage as a strategy to protect memory during stressful periods? ## 📖 Passage 2: Why Cities are Becoming Greener > Across the world, urban planners are working to make cities greener - not just by adding more parks and trees, but by rethinking how buildings, streets, and public spaces are designed. The motivation for this change comes from a combination of environmental, health, and economic concerns. Warmer summers, rising pollution levels, and growing public interest in sustainability have pushed city governments to take action. > > One increasingly popular strategy is the creation of "green roofs" - rooftops covered with vegetation. These surfaces help insulate buildings, reducing both heating and cooling costs, while also absorbing rainwater and filtering pollution from the air. Some cities have even passed laws requiring green roofs on new buildings above a certain size. In Copenhagen, for example, all new flat-roofed buildings must include some form of green roof, a policy credited with reducing the city's carbon emissions and improving air quality. > > Other strategies include the installation of "bioswales" - shallow drainage channels filled with plants that capture stormwater and reduce flooding - as well as the conversion of unused lots into community gardens. Critics point out that such projects can be expensive and may benefit wealthier neighborhoods more than poorer ones. Supporters, however, argue that when designed thoughtfully, greener cities can improve quality of life for residents across all income levels. The debate over how best to green a city continues, but the trend itself shows no sign of slowing down. ## Questions 6-10 (Passage 2)

questionText: What does the author conclude in the final paragraph? ## 📖 Passage 2: Why Some Languages Are Dying Out > Of the roughly 7,000 languages spoken in the world today, linguists estimate that nearly half are at risk of disappearing by the end of this century. A language is considered endangered when it is no longer being passed on to children, and it is called extinct when its last native speaker dies. Language loss has been accelerating in recent decades, driven by a combination of social, economic, and political pressures that favor dominant languages over smaller ones. > > Globalization has played a central role. In many countries, economic opportunities are concentrated in cities where a few major languages dominate. Young people who hope to find good jobs or access higher education often feel pressure to abandon their ancestral languages in favor of these more widely spoken tongues. Media and technology compound the effect: films, social networks, and educational software are predominantly produced in a handful of global languages, reducing exposure to minority ones. > > Some scholars have questioned whether the loss of individual languages really matters, arguing that fewer languages might make communication easier. Most linguists, however, strongly disagree. Each language, they argue, contains unique knowledge about the world, including detailed vocabulary for local plants, animals, and ecosystems that may not exist in any other language. Languages also carry cultural memory, poetry, and ways of thinking that cannot be fully translated. > > Efforts to preserve endangered languages have grown. Some communities have established schools where children learn in their ancestral language; others have created dictionaries, apps, and recordings of elders speaking. While these efforts cannot save every language, they demonstrate that language loss is not inevitable. When communities, linguists, and governments work together, even severely endangered languages can sometimes be revived. ## Questions 6-10 (Passage 2)

Clothing that once cost hundreds of dollars and was expected to last for years is now available for a fraction of the price, with new styles appearing in stores every few weeks. This phenomenon, known as "fast fashion," has made trendy clothing accessible to millions of consumers worldwide. Yet beneath the surface of cheap prices and endless variety lies a complex set of problems that few shoppers consider when making a purchase. > > The environmental impact of fast fashion is substantial. The industry is now responsible for roughly 10 percent of global carbon emissions, more than international flights and maritime shipping combined. Producing a single cotton T-shirt can require more than 2,000 liters of water, and the synthetic fabrics used in many fast-fashion garments shed microscopic plastic fibers that eventually find their way into oceans and drinking water. When clothes are worn only a few times before being discarded, as often happens with fast-fashion items, this environmental burden multiplies accordingly. > > The human cost is equally troubling. To produce clothes cheaply and quickly, many fast-fashion brands rely on factories in countries where labor is inexpensive and regulations are weak. Workers in these facilities, often young women, may work long hours for minimal pay in conditions that would not be tolerated in wealthier nations. Investigations have repeatedly revealed safety violations, unpaid wages, and even cases of forced labor within fast-fashion supply chains. While some major brands have pledged reforms, progress has been uneven and difficult to verify. > > In response, a growing movement of consumers is questioning the true value of cheap clothing. Some are turning to second-hand shopping, repairing old garments, or buying fewer but higher-quality items designed to last. Others are supporting brands that commit to transparent supply chains and sustainable materials. Governments in several countries have also begun considering regulations that would hold fashion companies accountable for their environmental and social impacts. Whether these efforts will be enough to transform the industry remains unclear, but awareness of fast fashion's hidden costs continues to grow.

She is one of the most talented musicians ______ I have ever heard. # 🛑 STOP! סיימת את כל 31 השאלות? לפני שמסתכלים על התשובות: 1. בדקו שענינו על כל השאלות 2. רשמו את הזמן הכולל שלקח לכם 3. רק עכשיו – עברו לחלק ההסברים ## 📝 Part 2: Answer Key and Explanations ### 🔹 פרק 1 – Sentence Completion #### ✅ Q1 – Correct Answer: (A) stuck ניתוח: "was ______ in traffic" - ביטוי נפוץ לציון הילכדות בפקק. - ✅ stuck in traffic = תקוע בפקק. Collocation קלאסי. - ❌ relaxed, excited, hungry - לא קשורים לתנועה/עיכוב. 💡 טיפ: stuck + מקום (traffic, elevator, snow) = Collocation קבוע. #### ✅ Q2 – Correct Answer: (B) reads ניתוח: "Every morning" = הרגל → הווה פשוט. "Father" = גוף שלישי יחיד → פועל + s. - ❌ read - צורת הבסיס; לרבים או משפט תלוי. - ✅ reads - הווה פשוט, יחיד. תקין. - ❌ reading - Gerund. - ❌ have read - Present Perfect (רבים / אני). #### ✅ Q3 – Correct Answer: (C) review ניתוח: "Teacher asked students to ___ essays before submitting" - מורה מבקש מהתלמידים לבדוק את החיבורים לפני הגשה. - ❌ forget, ignore, destroy - כולם שליליים, לא מה שמורה מבקש. - ✅ review = לבדוק, לעבור שוב. Collocation נפוץ לעבודה אקדמית. #### ✅ Q4 – Correct Answer: (C) insisted ניתוח: "Despite the cold weather" = ניגוד. הילדים, למרות הקור, רצו לצאת לשחק. - ❌ refused - סירבו. סותר; הם רצו לצאת. - ❌ failed - נכשלו. לא הגיוני. - ✅ insisted = התעקשו. מתאים לניגוד של "despite". - ❌ pretended - התחזו. לא מתאים. 💡 טיפ: insist on V-ing = להתעקש על. מבנה קבוע. ### 🔹 פרק 2 – Sentence Completion #### ✅ Q5 – Correct Answer: (C) so ניתוח: "Museum closed on Mondays ___ visitors should plan accordingly" - קשר של סיבה → תוצאה. - ❌ but - ניגוד. לא מתאים. - ❌ although - ניגוד. - ✅ so = לכן, כתוצאה מכך. נכון. - ❌ unless - תנאי שלילי. לא מתאים. #### ✅ Q6 – Correct Answer: (B) for ניתוח: "studying French ___ three years" - משך זמן (3 שנים). - ❌ since - נקודת זמן ("since 2020"). לא משך. - ✅ for = למשך (משך זמן). נכון. - ❌ during - בזמן (אירוע). לא מתאים. - ❌ while - בעוד. לא מתאים. 💡 טיפ: for + duration (for 3 years, for a week). since + point in time (since Monday, since 2020). #### ✅ Q7 – Correct Answer: (B) challenges ניתוח: "New theory ___ many long-held assumptions" - תיאוריה חדשה לרוב מאתגרת אמונות ישנות. - ❌ supports - תומכת. אם תומכת, היא לא מעניינת כחדשה. - ✅ challenges = מאתגרת, מערערת. מתאים לחדשנות. - ❌ ignores - מתעלמת. תיאוריה לא "מתעלמת". - ❌ celebrates - חוגגת. לא הגיוני בהקשר מדעי. #### ✅ Q8 – Correct Answer: (B) substantially ניתוח: "Profits increased ___ over past 5 years" - מתאר עלייה משמעותית. - ❌ rarely - נדיר. לא תואר של עלייה. - ✅ substantially = באופן משמעותי. Collocation נפוץ בכלכלה. - ❌ occasionally - מדי פעם. לא מתאים להגדרת גודל. - ❌ never - אף פעם. סותר "increased". 💡 טיפ: עלייה/ירידה + adverb של גודל: substantially, significantly, considerably, moderately. ### 🔹 פרק 3 – Reading Comprehension #### ✅ Q9 – Correct Answer: (B) סוג: Main Idea. ניתוח: הקטע בנוי סביב הניגוד בין היתרון (מחירים נמוכים, גיוון) לחסרונות (סביבה, זכויות עובדים). התשובה חייבת לתפוס את שני הצדדים. - ❌ (A) "more affordable and accessible" - רק חצי מהרעיון. - ✅ (B) "cheap prices but carries significant environmental and human costs" - תופס את שני הצדדים. - ❌ (C) "most polluting in the world" - מוגזם; הקטע אומר 10% של פליטות, לא "הכי מזהם". - ❌ (D) "never buy any new clothing" - לא נאמר ולא רמוז. #### ✅ Q10 – Correct Answer: (B) סוג: Specific Detail. איפה בקטע: פסקה 2: "The industry is now responsible for roughly 10 percent of global carbon emissions". #### ✅ Q11 – Correct Answer: (B) סוג: Specific Detail. איפה בקטע: פסקה 3: "Workers in these facilities, often young women, may work long hours for minimal pay in conditions that would not be tolerated in wealthier nations." - ❌ (A) "rising prices" - הפוך;
